newsitem.title: USA: CME pork futures rise on Russia buying rumors.
newsitem.headline: CME pork futures rise on Russia buying rumors.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures sped higher in late trading on rumors Russia bought about six million lbs of hog carcasses, CME traders said.
A U.S. Meat Export Federation official said he was checking with export sources but could not confirm the rumors.
One livestock analyst said the recent drop in CME pork prices may have encouraged Russia to buy now.

"I'd say there is a better than 50-to-50 chance that rumors concerning Russia being interested in purchasing six million to seven million lbs of hog carcasses is true," said Chuck Levitt, livestock analyst with Alaron Trading Corp.
At 1255 CDT, CME October lean hog futures were up 0.375 at 70.225 cents per lb and December hogs were up 0.700 at 67.250. CME February pork bellies were up 1.050 cents at 71.000.
Some traders said the recent drop in hog futures may have prompted Russia to enter the market. CME October hogs have dropped from 76.00 cents on August 4 to 69.850 early Tuesday.
